text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000565 bills 99215 above expectation in every complexity tier, including simple acute visits, but the few charts returned support the level billed, so the documentation is too thin to decide.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not confined to sicker patients. The 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider rate in every condition-count tier, and most other visits are billed at 99214, which looks more like a practice-wide coding habit than a complex panel. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s for routine acute problems on patients with no chronic conditions, such as upper respiratory infection (C0278247, C0279743), UTI (C0278238 is a rash; C0279630, C0278859 and C0279987 are UTIs) and low back pain (C0280178), which are hard to square with high-level MDM. Weighing against this, both documented 99215s (C0279632, C0279705) support high MDM, no documented claim fell below its billed level, and every note claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had a matching lab or test line. Two charts out of more than two hundred 99215s cannot confirm or clear the pattern, so a reviewer should first request targeted records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, and check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity decision-making or templated or cloned language."}
